title: Carpano Sweet Vermouth
about: Sweet red vermouth starts here. In 1786 Antonio Benedetto Carpano, in a wine shop opposite the Royal Palace in Turin, blended herbs and spices with muscat wine and launched what is generally held to be the first commercial vermouth; King Vittorio Amedeo III adopted it for the royal household, and between 1840 and 1888 a glass of Carpano was Turin’s aperitif of choice. The family business moved to a factory in 1898, was sold to Silvio Turati in 1939, and in 2001 passed to Fratelli Branca of Milan, who make it today.

Carpano makes more than one sweet red vermouth. Carpano Classico Rosso descends from the 1786 recipe, with only technical changes for stability: white wine, lightly fortified and sweetened, infused with aromatic herbs and spices including wormwood, cinnamon, clove and citrus, at 16%. Antica Formula, also traced to the original recipe, is richer and vanilla-scented, at 16.5% in individually numbered bottles. Punt e Mes, created in 1870, adds “a point and a half” of bitterness, a name said to come from a stockbroker’s order at the Carpano bar.

Carpano’s rosso is ruby red, with wormwood, clove and cinnamon on the nose, lifted by citrus. On the palate it is full and sweet with a light bitter edge, and a long finish of vanilla, caramel and sweet spice. In Turin it is drunk as an aperitivo, over ice with a splash of soda, and it is the backbone of the Negroni, the Americano and the Manhattan.
facts: White wine, lightly fortified and sweetened
Wormwood, cinnamon, clove, citrus and other herbs and spices
Over ice with a splash of soda, or in a Negroni or Manhattan
